items.prompt:
Read the two stories below.

Story A: 'Sam loves to swim. Every summer he goes to the pool and swims laps.'

Story B: 'Emma loves to swim. Every summer she goes to the lake and swims with her friends.'

What is the same about Sam and Emma?
items.answer: Both Sam and Emma love to swim and both go swimming every summer.

steps: Look for what both characters share: they both love to swim.
Both swim in summer — same season and same activity.
Use 'both' to write the similarity.

items.prompt:
Read the two stories below.

Story A: 'The tortoise walked slowly but never stopped. He reached the finish line last, but he reached it.'

Story B: 'The hare ran fast. He took a nap halfway through the race. He woke up too late. The tortoise had already won.'

How are the tortoise and the hare different in this story?
items.answer: The tortoise is slow but steady and never gives up. The hare is fast but stops to take a nap and loses. They are different in speed and in how much effort they put into finishing.

steps: Tortoise: slow, steady, does not stop = persistent.
Hare: fast, takes a nap, misses his chance = overconfident.
These are opposite traits that lead to opposite results.

items.prompt:
Read the two stories below.

Story A (Cinderella, European): 'Cinderella's fairy godmother gave her a gown and glass slippers and sent her to the royal ball in a pumpkin carriage. She danced with the prince.'

Story B (Yeh-Shen, Chinese): 'The bones of Yeh-Shen's magical fish gave her a gown and golden shoes so she could attend the king's festival. She danced and the king noticed her.'

Name one thing that is the same in both stories.
items.answer: In both stories, the main character receives a magical gown and special shoes and attends a celebration where she dances and a royal person notices her.

steps: Look for the same events in both stories.
Both characters: receive magical clothes and shoes, attend a celebration, are noticed by a royal person.
These are parallel elements in two Cinderella-type stories from different cultures.

items.prompt:
Read the two stories below.

Story A: 'Nico was nervous about performing in the school play. He practiced his lines every night. On the night of the show, he forgot one line. He took a breath and kept going. The audience clapped.

Story B: 'Dani was nervous about her violin recital. She practiced every day after school. At the recital, she hit one wrong note. She froze for a second, then started again. The audience clapped.'

Both Nico and Dani make a mistake during a performance. What is the same about how they each respond to their mistake?
items.answer: Both Nico and Dani make a small mistake, pause briefly, and then continue with their performance. Both recover and finish, and both receive applause at the end. Their responses show resilience — the ability to keep going after a setback.

steps: Both characters make a mistake mid-performance.
Nico: forgets a line, takes a breath, keeps going.
Dani: hits a wrong note, freezes, starts again.
Both pause but both recover and finish.
Both receive applause — both succeed despite the mistake.

items.prompt:
Read the two stories below.

Story A: 'In a Lakota tale, the spider Iktomi was clever and always tried to trick others. One day he tried to trick the ducks into closing their eyes and dancing. He planned to grab them. But one duck peeked and saw what he was doing. She cried out and the ducks flew away.'

Story B: 'In a Greek tale, the god Hermes was clever and a trickster too. He stole Apollo's cattle when he was just a baby, hiding them in a cave. Apollo was furious. But Zeus made them work out a trade: the cattle for a lyre Hermes had invented.'

Both Iktomi and Hermes are tricksters. What is different about the outcome of their tricks?
items.answer: Iktomi's trick fails completely — one duck sees through it and the plan is ruined. He gets nothing. Hermes's trick is discovered, but he finds a way to turn it into a deal — he trades his invention (the lyre) for the cattle. Hermes ends up with a good outcome even after being caught. Iktomi is outwitted; Hermes talks his way into a success.

steps: Both characters are tricksters who try to steal or deceive.
Iktomi: trick is discovered, ducks escape, he fails completely.
Hermes: theft is discovered, but he negotiates a trade and benefits.
Different outcomes: Iktomi = failure; Hermes = successful deal despite being caught.
This also shows a character difference: Iktomi is outwitted; Hermes is clever enough to recover.

items.prompt:
Read the two stories below.

Story A: 'Grandpa Chen moved to a new town when he was sixty. He did not know anyone. He started going to the community garden every morning. Over months, he learned everyone's name. He brought seeds from his home country to share. By the end of summer, he had more friends than he could count.'

Story B: 'Mrs. Rivera moved to a new town when she was sixty. She did not know anyone. She was nervous to go out. Her daughter visited and said, "Come to my cooking class." Mrs. Rivera went once, then twice, then every week. She found her people in the kitchen.'

Both Grandpa Chen and Mrs. Rivera are new in town and find community. How is the way each one finds community different?
items.answer: Grandpa Chen actively goes out on his own every morning and builds community through consistent presence and generosity — sharing seeds from his home country. Mrs. Rivera is more hesitant and only goes out because her daughter encourages her. She finds her community through a structured activity (a cooking class) that was chosen for her. Grandpa Chen is self-directed; Mrs. Rivera needs a push and a structured setting.

steps: Both are new to town, both find community — same outcome.
Grandpa Chen: goes out on his own every morning, takes initiative, shares seeds.
Mrs. Rivera: hesitant, only goes because her daughter suggests it, finds friends in a class.
Contrast: self-directed (Grandpa) vs. needs encouragement and structure (Mrs. Rivera).
Both succeed, but through different paths.

items.prompt:
Read the two stories below.

Story A (Aesop's fable): 'A grasshopper played and sang all summer while the ant worked hard storing food. When winter came, the grasshopper was cold and hungry. He begged the ant for food. The ant said, "You played all summer. Now dance." And closed the door.'

Story B (A retelling): 'A grasshopper played and sang all summer while the ant worked. When winter came, the grasshopper was cold and hungry. The ant looked at him for a long moment. Then she said, "Come in. But next summer, work with me." The grasshopper agreed, and the following summer he helped store food. He never went hungry again.'

These are two versions of the same fable. What is the same and what is different, and what is different about the lesson each version teaches? Use evidence from both passages.
items.answer: Same: Both versions begin identically — a grasshopper plays all summer while the ant works, and when winter comes the grasshopper is hungry and must ask the ant for help. The problem and setup are the same. Different: In Story A, the ant refuses to help and sends the grasshopper away with a cold lesson: face the consequences of your choices. In Story B, the ant takes the grasshopper in but gives him a condition: work with me next summer. The grasshopper agrees and reforms. Different lessons: Story A teaches that laziness has consequences and you cannot expect others to save you. Story B teaches that compassion combined with accountability can change someone — it is more about second chances and rehabilitation than punishment. Story A's lesson is harsher and more individual; Story B's is more community-minded and forgiving.

steps: Same: grasshopper plays, ant works, winter comes, grasshopper asks for help.
Different: ant refuses in A; ant helps with a condition in B.
Lesson in A: face consequences of laziness — you reap what you sow.
Lesson in B: compassion + accountability can change behavior — second chances matter.
A values individual responsibility; B values community and forgiveness.
Same story, different values — this is what cultural variation in folk tales looks like.

items.prompt:
Read the two stories below.

Story A (Inuit tale): 'Kiviuq was a great wanderer. He paddled his kayak across endless seas, always moving. He survived storms, monsters, and the tricks of evil spirits. He was never allowed to rest for long. Some say he still paddles today, searching for something he cannot name.'

Story B (Greek myth): 'Odysseus spent ten years trying to get home after the Trojan War. He fought monsters, escaped a witch, resisted the Sirens, and lost many men. At last he reached Ithaca. He put down his oar. He was finally home.'

Both Kiviuq and Odysseus are wandering heroes on long journeys full of danger. Analyze what is the same AND what is different about their journeys and what each story says about what the hero is searching for.
items.answer: Same: Both Kiviuq and Odysseus are great heroes who travel on water for an extraordinarily long time, face supernatural threats (monsters, evil spirits), and demonstrate extraordinary endurance. Both are figures of resilience who survive when others would not. Different: Odysseus has a clear destination — home. His journey is defined by loss and longing and ends in arrival and reunion. Kiviuq has no named destination — he wanders endlessly and some say he is still paddling today. His journey has no end and no resolution. What they search for is different: Odysseus searches for home (belonging, family, rest); Kiviuq searches for 'something he cannot name' — which may represent the human search for meaning itself. Odysseus's story is about the power of homecoming; Kiviuq's is about the nature of endless longing and the restlessness of the human spirit. Both are heroic, but Odysseus's heroism ends in peace while Kiviuq's continues forever.

steps: Same: water journey, monsters and supernatural threats, extraordinary endurance, hero survives.
Different: Odysseus has a clear goal (home); Kiviuq has no named goal.
Odysseus's journey ends in arrival and rest; Kiviuq's never ends.
What they search for: Odysseus = home, belonging; Kiviuq = something unnamed, perhaps meaning or peace.
Theme in Odysseus's story: the hero can come home — endurance is rewarded with rest.
Theme in Kiviuq's story: some quests have no end — the search is itself the life.
Both stories reflect deep truths about the human journey, but through different cultural understandings.
